microtheory.name: syntax_linguistics
microtheory.definition: Sentence structure — constituents, dependencies, word order, agreement, transformations. Major frameworks: Chomsky's generative (phrase-structure, X-bar, minimalism), dependency grammar (Tesnière), construction grammar (Goldberg), categorial grammar (Lambek). Substrate analogue: the grammar over substrate's lexical concepts that produces well-formed messages.

concepts.name: constituent
concepts.definition: Group of words functioning as a syntactic unit. Tests: substitution, movement, coordination. Substrate analogue: substrate's compositional concept group.

concepts.name: phrase_structure_grammar
concepts.definition: Chomsky 1957. Rewrite rules: S → NP VP. Generates tree structures. Substrate analogue: substrate's hierarchical Term-tree generation.

concepts.name: noun_phrase
concepts.definition: NP. Headed by noun, may include determiner, adjectives, modifiers. Substrate analogue: substrate's object-referent compositional structure.

concepts.name: verb_phrase
concepts.definition: VP. Headed by verb, includes objects + adjuncts. Substrate analogue: substrate's action-referent compositional structure.

concepts.name: x_bar_theory
concepts.definition: Jackendoff 1977, Chomsky. All phrases share template: head + complement + specifier. XP → Spec X'; X' → X Complement. Substrate analogue: substrate's universal compositional template.

concepts.name: syntactic_tree
concepts.definition: Hierarchical representation of constituent structure. Nodes = constituents; leaves = words. Substrate analogue: substrate's Term-tree.

concepts.name: head
concepts.definition: Word that determines the phrase's category + properties. Noun heads NP, verb heads VP. Substrate analogue: substrate's category-defining concept.

concepts.name: dependent
concepts.definition: Word whose properties depend on another. Modifier, complement, specifier. Substrate analogue: substrate's dependent-edge concept.

concepts.name: complement
concepts.definition: Required dependent of a head. 'Throw' requires direct object. Substrate analogue: substrate's required-relation concept.

concepts.name: adjunct
concepts.definition: Optional modifier. Prepositional phrases, adverbs. Substrate analogue: substrate's optional-relation concept.

concepts.name: specifier
concepts.definition: Element that introduces the phrase. Determiner for NP, auxiliary for VP. Substrate analogue: substrate's phrase-initiator concept.

concepts.name: word_order_typology
concepts.definition: SOV (Japanese, 45%), SVO (English, 41%), VSO (Welsh, 9%), others rare. Greenberg's universals correlate with other features. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-language constituent-order parameter.

concepts.name: subject
concepts.definition: Privileged argument. Typically agent, agreed with by verb, undergoes passivization. Substrate analogue: substrate's agent-role concept.

concepts.name: object
concepts.definition: Argument of transitive verb. Direct vs indirect. Patient/theme role. Substrate analogue: substrate's patient-role concept.

concepts.name: thematic_role
concepts.definition: Semantic role: agent, patient, theme, recipient, instrument, location. Bound to syntactic positions. Substrate analogue: substrate's edge-type semantics.

concepts.name: agreement
concepts.definition: Morphological covariation between elements. Verb agrees with subject in person + number. Substrate analogue: substrate's cross-concept consistency constraint.

concepts.name: case_marking
concepts.definition: Morphological marking of grammatical role. Nominative + accusative (English pronouns); ergative-absolutive (Basque, Inuktitut). Substrate analogue: substrate's role-marker encoding.

concepts.name: tense_aspect_mood
concepts.definition: TAM. Verb morphology encoding time, completion, modality. Substrate analogue: substrate's event-temporal-modal attributes.

concepts.name: transformation
concepts.definition: Chomsky 1957. Operations relating deep + surface structure. Passive, question, topicalization. Substrate analogue: substrate's structural rewriting operation.

concepts.name: movement
concepts.definition: Element displaced from canonical position leaves trace. Wh-movement, NP-movement. Substrate analogue: substrate's reference-link spanning structural distance.

concepts.name: binding_theory
concepts.definition: Chomsky 1981. Principles A/B/C governing anaphora — reflexives bound locally, pronouns bound non-locally, R-expressions free. Substrate analogue: substrate's reference-resolution constraints.

concepts.name: minimalist_program
concepts.definition: Chomsky 1995. Reduce syntax to two operations: Merge + Move. Economy + interface conditions. Substrate analogue: substrate's parsimonious compositional grammar.

concepts.name: dependency_grammar
concepts.definition: Tesnière 1959. Sentence as directed graph of head-dependent relations. Used in modern NLP. Substrate analogue: substrate's relational graph view.

concepts.name: categorial_grammar
concepts.definition: Lambek 1958. Syntactic categories as functors. Computes via combinators. Substrate analogue: substrate's typed-function composition.

concepts.name: head_driven_phrase_structure_grammar
concepts.definition: HPSG. Pollard + Sag 1994. Unification-based. Substrate analogue: substrate's feature-structure unification.

concepts.name: tree_adjoining_grammar
concepts.definition: TAG. Joshi 1985. Generates by adjoining elementary trees. Substrate analogue: substrate's tree-rewriting grammar.

rules.name: constituents_pass_substitution_test
rules.head: the substrate hypothesises a constituent
rules.body: the test is whether it can be replaced by a single word + still be grammatical. Substrate's compositional-unit detection.

rules.name: x_bar_provides_universal_template
rules.head: the substrate parses a phrase of any category
rules.body: the structure follows X-bar: specifier-head-complement. Substrate's universal compositional template.

rules.name: subject_verb_agreement_enforced_locally
rules.head: the substrate produces or parses a sentence with subject + verb
rules.body: agreement in person + number must hold. Cross-language variation in specifics. Substrate's local consistency check.

rules.name: movement_leaves_trace
rules.head: the substrate sees an element in a non-canonical position
rules.body: a trace remains in the canonical position; reference between trace + moved element must be tracked. Substrate's long-distance dependency.

rules.name: word_order_correlates_with_typological_features
rules.head: the substrate identifies the dominant word order
rules.body: other typological features predicted by Greenberg's universals. SOV → postpositions; SVO → prepositions. Substrate's typological consistency.
